key_facts: MRI provides high soft-tissue contrast and is especially useful for brain anatomy.
The skull often appears dark on MRI because cortical bone has very low signal.
Gray matter and white matter are distinguishable by signal intensity differences, depending on the sequence.
The lateral ventricles contain cerebrospinal fluid and are commonly visible on brain MRI.
